audit.why: 59.46% over 74 games. The chart gives Yasuo levels 3, 4-5 and both item stages while Akshan holds level 1 and level 6; the prose calls the mid-lane stretch 'this is your lane', which is slightly rosier than the chart but the poke advantage is real and I left ratings alone.
Lvl 2-3 poke, Lvl 6 Comeuppance, Youmuu's, and Yasuo's crit scaling. Correct four; only the Yasuo-side spike needed its mechanism fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) The entry knows Wind Wall eats Avengerang and the passive second shot, but never says it also eats the shots Heroic Swing fires while swinging — and mid actively recommends 'hook off terrain to swing and fire while moving' as the safe pattern. Every one of those shots is a projectile. (2) The entry says 'his R knockup' three times. Last Breath does not knock up; it BLINKS to an already-Airborne champion. The knockup comes from Steel Tempest at two stacks of Gathering Storm.
audit.why: Riot's text for Wind Wall: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', 25/23/21/19/17s, 400 range. Riot's text for Heroic Swing: he 'swings around it, repeatedly firing at the nearest enemy' — Akshan's kit flags P, Q, E and R as projectiles, so the wall blanks his whole kit, swing included. Riot's text for Last Breath: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion... holding all Airborne enemies in the area in the air.' Akshan has no self-knockup, so Yasuo can only ult him off his own two-stack Steel Tempest tornado or an ally's CC. Counting Q stacks is the actual read, and the page never mentioned it.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall (25s at rank 1, 4s duration) blocks Avengerang, the passive shot, Comeuppance AND the shots fired mid-Heroic-Swing. Last Breath needs you Airborne first, which in a 1v1 means the two-stack Steel Tempest tornado — count his Q stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Its long cooldown' appears four times with no number attached.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and stands for 4 seconds. Against a 9s Avengerang that is a concrete, repeatable trade rhythm: bait, wait four, then own the next twenty-one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two useful mechanics absent: Yasuo's Flow shield and the Sweeping Blade re-cast restriction.
audit.why: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield whenever he is moving, which is why poke chip under-performs against a Yasuo who never stands still. And Sweeping Blade 'cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds', so once he dashes onto you he cannot immediately dash back off you — that is your window, not his.

edits.after: Feint a single Q to bait Wind Wall, then commit double-shot trades across the 25s before it comes back

edits.before: Survive to 2+ crit items where R knockup and Phantom Dancer let him all-in your squishy frame
edits.after: Stack two Steel Tempests for the tornado — that knockup is the only way Last Breath reaches you

edits.before: Yasuo's window — IE/Phantom Dancer crit and his R knockup let him E through the wave and crit-combo your squishy, shieldless frame down before R can answer.
edits.after: Yasuo's window — IE/Phantom Dancer crit, and the two-stack Steel Tempest tornado is what makes you Airborne for Last Breath, so count his Q stacks, not his ult icon.

edits.before: Yasuo's Windwall (W) is the whole early game — it eats your Q boomerang AND your passive second shot (both projectiles), so never throw a Q into a Yasuo holding W. Feint with one Q from max range to draw it, then step up and double-shot trade while W sits on its long cooldown; your passive plus Q out-chips a Level 1-2 Yasuo who can only farm by E-dashing minion to minion. Watch his Sweeping Blade dashes — if he's spent them last-hitting, he can't gap-close or escape, and that's your window to walk up, land the third-stack proc, and grab your shield.
edits.after: Yasuo's Wind Wall (W) is the whole early game — it eats your Q boomerang, your passive second shot AND the shots you fire mid-Heroic-Swing, because every one is a projectile. Never throw into a Yasuo holding it. Feint one Q from max range to draw the wall, wait out its 4 seconds, then own the 25 it takes to return. His Flow shield builds whenever he moves, so chip lands softer than the numbers look. And Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same target for a few seconds — once he dashes onto you, he cannot dash straight back off.

edits.before: This is your lane. With E (Heroic Swing) at 3 and the passive double-shot online, you out-range and out-poke him — boomerang the wave, hook off terrain to swing and fire while moving, and chip him low without ever standing still for his Q tornado. At 6, R (Comeuppance) is your finisher: channel it when he dashes in chunked, because the up-to-200% missing-HP scaling executes a low Yasuo who commits an E onto you. Your Youmuu's first-item spike plus the 0.5s E reset on a takedown is where you snowball, and W's near-terrain camo lets you reset and roam.
edits.after: This is your lane. With E (Heroic Swing) at 3 and the double-shot online you out-range and out-poke him — boomerang the wave, hook off terrain, and chip him low without standing still for a Steel Tempest tornado. But the swing fires projectiles too, so a Wind Wall laid across your arc blanks the whole thing: open it only once the 25s wall is spent. At 6, Comeuppance executes a chunked Yasuo who dashes in — and it is a projectile as well, so never fire it into a standing wall. Youmuu's plus the 0.5s E reset is where you snowball.

edits.before: Yasuo flips the script at 2+ items and you cannot brawl him there — once he has Infinity Edge and Phantom Dancer he E-dashes onto you through the wave, blocks your R or Q with Windwall, and his R knockup chains a full crit combo onto your shieldless squishy frame. You have to close the lane before that: snowball your early-mid poke lead into plates and roams so the game never reaches his scaling. Late, hold space, fire R from max range only when his Windwall is on cooldown, and never let him E-gap onto you with his ult up.
edits.after: Yasuo flips the script at 2+ items and you cannot brawl him there — once he has Infinity Edge and Phantom Dancer he dashes onto you through the wave, and Wind Wall blocks your Q, your Comeuppance and your swing shots alike, since all three are projectiles. Two Steel Tempest stacks make the tornado that lets Last Breath reach you at all, so count them. Close the lane first: snowball your early-mid poke lead into plates and roams. Late, hold space, fire R only once the 25s wall is spent, and never let him gap onto you.

edits.before: E (Heroic Swing) at 3 lets you hook off terrain and fire while swinging at angles his Sweeping Blade can't punish — pure poke dominance.
edits.after: Heroic Swing at 3 fires while you arc off terrain — but those shots are projectiles too, so a Wind Wall across the arc blanks the whole swing.

edits.before: He out-scales hard: IE/Phantom Dancer crit and his R knockup let him E onto your squishy frame and delete you — play back and let your team handle him.
edits.after: He out-scales hard: IE/Phantom Dancer crit, and Last Breath only reaches you off his own two-stack Q tornado — count Steel Tempest stacks, not his ult icon.

notes: This is the Azir-vs-Yasuo error in a different costume. The entry correctly warned that Wind Wall eats Avengerang and the passive second shot, then in the very next paragraph recommended hooking off terrain to 'swing and fire while moving' as the safe pattern — Heroic Swing's shots are projectiles too, so a wall across the arc blanks the entire swing, and Comeuppance likewise. Now stated in early, mid, late and whys[2]. Second fix: the page said 'his R knockup' three times, but Last Breath blinks to an ALREADY-Airborne target — in a 1v1 the only source is his own two-stack Steel Tempest tornado, so the real read is counting Gathering Storm stacks rather than watching his ultimate. Added the 25s/4s Wind Wall numbers, the Flow shield, and the Sweeping Blade same-target re-cast lockout.
